zh: 2010年英语专业全国统一考试。

en: Grade eight.
zh: 专业八级。

en: Part I Listening Comprehension.
zh: 第一部分：听力理解。

en: Section A mini-lecture.
zh: A节：短讲。

en: In this section you will hear a mini-lecture.
zh: 在这一节中，你将听到一段短讲。

en: You will hear the mini-lecture once only.
zh: 这段短讲只播放一遍。

en: While listening to the mini-lecture, please complete the gap-filling task on Answer Sheet I, and write no more than three words for each gap.
zh: 请边听短讲，边完成答题卡一上的填空任务；每空填写不超过三个词。

en: Make sure the word or words you fill in is or are both grammatically and semantically acceptable.
zh: 请确保填入的词在语法和语义上都恰当。

en: You may use the blank sheet for note-taking.
zh: 你可以用空白纸做笔记。

en: You have 30 seconds to preview the gap-filling task.
zh: 你有三十秒钟预览填空任务。

en: Now listen to the mini-lecture.
zh: 现在请听短讲。

en: When it is over, you will be given Three minutes to check your work.
zh: 短讲结束后，你将有三分钟检查作答。

en: Paralinguistic Features of Language.
zh: 语言的副语言特征。

en: Good morning, everyone.
zh: 大家早上好。

en: Today we’ll continue our discussion on describing language.
zh: 今天我们继续讨论如何描述语言。

en: Last week we examined such features of, of language as grammar, vocabulary, the sounds of language, etc.
zh: 上周，我们考察了语法、词汇、语音等语言特征。

en: In this lecture, we’ll look at another important aspect of language.
zh: 这堂课，我们要了解语言的另一个重要方面。

en: Perhaps some of you may wonder what is this important aspect of language.
zh: 也许有人会想，这个重要方面到底是什么呢？

en: Let me tell you.
zh: 我来告诉大家。

en: It refers to features of communication that takes place without the use of grammar or vocabulary.
zh: 它指的是那些不借助语法或词汇而实现的交流特征。

en: They are called “paralinguistic features of language”.
zh: 它们被称为“语言的副语言特征”。

en: These features fall into two broad categories: those that involve the voice and those that involve the body.
zh: 这些特征大致分成两类：一类与声音有关，另一类与身体有关。

en: Now, the first category is what we call vocal paralinguistic features.
zh: 第一类，就是我们所说的声音副语言特征。

en: Vocal features are actually tones of voice.
zh: 声音特征实际上就是不同的语气或声调。

en: While they are, perhaps, not central to meaning in communication in the same way as grammar or vocabulary,
zh: 虽然它们可能不像语法或词汇那样处于交流意义的核心，

en: they may, nevertheless, convey attitude or intention in some way.
zh: 却仍然能够在某种程度上传达态度或意图。

en: Let me give you some examples.
zh: 我来举几个例子。

en: The first is whispering, which indicates the need for secrecy.
zh: 第一个例子是低声说话，这表明有保密的需要。

en: The second is breathiness.
zh: 第二个是带有气息的说话声。

en: This is to show deep emotion.
zh: 这是为了表达强烈的感情。

en: The third is huskiness, which is to show unimportance.
zh: 第三个是沙哑的声音，用来表示事情并不重要。

en: The fourth is nasality.
zh: 第四个是鼻音。

en: This, um, is to indicate anxiety.
zh: 这，嗯，是用来表达焦虑的。

en: The last is extra lip rounding, which expresses greater intimacy, especially with babies, for example.
zh: 最后一个例子是把嘴唇拢得更圆，这表示更加亲昵，例如人们对婴儿说话时就会这样。

en: So we can see that there are a number of ways of altering our tone of voice and when we do this consciously, we do it to create different effects in communication.
zh: 因此，我们可以看到，改变语气的方式有很多；有意识地这样做，是为了在交流中产生不同的效果。

en: Now, let’s come to the second category, physical paralinguistic features, which involves the body.
zh: 现在我们来讲第二类，也就是与身体有关的身体副语言特征。

en: In addition to conveying meanings with tone of voice, we can also express our intention through the ways in which we use our bodies.
zh: 除了通过语气传达意义，我们还可以通过运用身体的方式表达意图。

en: You may ask: what are the ways, then?
zh: 你们也许会问，那么具体有哪些方式呢？

en: Let me cite some brief examples.
zh: 我来简单举几个例子。

en: The expression on our face, the gestures we make and even proximity or way we sit,
zh: 面部表情、手势，甚至我们与别人之间的距离或坐姿，

en: are some of the ways we send powerful messages about how we feel, or what we mean.
zh: 都能有力地传达自己的感受或意思。

en: Let me explain some of these in more detail.
zh: 我来进一步解释其中的几项。

en: First, facial expression.
zh: 首先是面部表情。

en: Facial expression is a powerful conveyer of meaning.
zh: 面部表情是传达意义的有力方式。

en: We all know smiling is an almost universal signal of pleasure or welcome.
zh: 我们都知道，微笑几乎是表示愉快或欢迎的通用信号。

en: But there are other facial expressions that may not be so common.
zh: 不过，也有一些面部表情没有那么普遍。

en: For instance, raising eye-brows suggests that you are surprised or interested in something.
zh: 例如，扬起眉毛表示你对某件事感到惊讶或感兴趣。

en: Other facial actions, such as biting your lip, which indicates that you are deep in thinking, or are uncertain about something;
zh: 其他面部动作，比如咬嘴唇，表示你在深思或对某事拿不准；

en: compressing the lips, which show that you are making decisions;
zh: 抿紧嘴唇表示你在作决定；

en: and a visible clenching of the teeth, to show that you are angry, are all powerful conveyers of meaning, too.
zh: 明显地咬紧牙齿，则表示你很生气。这些动作也都能有力地传达意义。

en: The second in this category is gesture.
zh: 这一类中的第二项是手势。

en: You see, we use gesture to indicate a wide range of meanings, though I have to emphasize that the actual gestures we use may be specific to particular cultures.
zh: 你看，我们用手势来表达各种各样的意思，不过我要强调，具体的手势可能只属于某些特定文化。

en: That is to say different cultures have their own favorite gestures in conveying meaning.
zh: 也就是说，不同文化各有自己惯用的手势来传达意思。

en: Here, a few examples may show you how powerful gestures can be.
zh: 下面的几个例子，可以说明手势能发挥多大的作用。

en: In British English behavior, shrugging shoulders may indicate an attitude of “I don’t care”, or “I don’t know”.
zh: 在英国人的行为习惯中，耸肩可能表示“我不在乎”或“我不知道”。

en: Crossing your arms may indicate relaxation.
zh: 交叉双臂可能表示放松。

en: But it can also powerfully show you are bored.
zh: 但这个动作也可能非常明确地表示你感到厌烦。

en: Waving can mean welcome and farewell whereas scratching your head may indicate that you are at a loss.
zh: 挥手可以表示欢迎或告别，而挠头则可能表示你不知所措。

en: In other cultures, placing your hand upon your heart is to indicate that you are telling the truth.
zh: 在其他一些文化中，把手放在心口表示自己在说实话。

en: Pointing your finger at your nose means it’s a secret.
zh: 用手指指着自己的鼻子，表示这是个秘密。

en: That’s why we say that gestures are culture-bound.
zh: 因此，我们说手势受文化的制约。

en: The third is proximity, posture and echoing.
zh: 第三项是距离、姿态和姿态呼应。

en: Proximity refers to the physical distance between speakers.
zh: 距离是指交谈者之间的身体距离。

en: This can indicate a number of things and can also be used to consciously send messages about intent.
zh: 它能够表达多种意思，也可以用来有意识地传达意图。

en: Closeness, for example, indicates intimacy or threat to many speakers.
zh: 例如，对许多交谈者而言，距离近表示亲密，也可能表示威胁。

en: But distance may show formality, or lack of interest.
zh: 而保持距离可能表示拘谨有礼，或缺乏兴趣。

en: Once again, I’d like to say, proximity is also both a matter of personal style, and is often culture-bound.
zh: 我想再次强调，人际距离既与个人风格有关，也常常受到文化制约。

en: So, what may seem normal to a speaker from one culture may appear unnecessarily close or distant to a speaker from another.
zh: 因此，对某种文化背景的交谈者而言很正常的距离，在另一种文化背景的人看来，可能显得过近或过远。

en: And standing close to someone may be quite appropriate in some situations such as an informal party,
zh: 站得离别人很近，在非正式聚会等场合可能很合适，

en: but completely out of place in other situations, such as a meeting with a superior.
zh: 但在与上级开会等场合，就可能完全不妥。

en: Next, posture.
zh: 接下来讲姿态。

en: Posture means the way in which someone holds his or her body, especially the back, shoulders and head, when standing, walking or sitting.
zh: 姿态是指一个人在站立、行走或坐着时，身体，尤其是背部、肩部和头部所保持的姿势。

en: A few examples.
zh: 下面举几个例子。

en: Hunched shoulders and a hanging head give a powerful indication of whether the person is happy or not.
zh: 耸缩的肩膀和低垂的头，能明显反映一个人是否开心。

en: A lowered head when speaking to a superior, with or without eye contact, can convey the appropriate relationship in some cultures.
zh: 在某些文化中，与上级交谈时低下头，无论有没有眼神接触，都能恰当地体现双方的关系。

en: On the other hand, direct level eye contact changes the nature of the interaction, and can be seen as either open or challenging.
zh: 另一方面，平视对方的直接眼神接触，会改变互动的性质，既可能被理解为坦诚，也可能被理解为挑战。

en: Last, echoing.
zh: 最后讲姿态呼应。

en: Now, what is echoing?
zh: 那么，什么是姿态呼应呢？

en: Let me start with an example.
zh: 我先举个例子。

en: Some of you may have noticed this phenomenon in your experience.
zh: 你们中有些人也许在自己的经历中注意到过这种现象。

en: When two people are keen to agree with each other, they would likely, though unconsciously, adopt the same posture, as if in imitation of each other.
zh: 当两个人很想与对方达成一致时，往往会不自觉地采用相同的姿态，仿佛在相互模仿。

en: They sit or stand in the same manner.
zh: 他们会以相同的方式坐着或站着。

en: When used in this way, echoing appears to complement the verbal communication.
zh: 以这种方式运用时，姿态呼应似乎能对言语交流起补充作用。

en: Of course, when such imitation is carried out consciously, it often indicates that someone is mocking at another speaker.
zh: 当然，如果这种模仿是有意为之，通常就表示一个人在嘲弄另一位交谈者。

en: OK. In today’s lecture, we looked at some paralinguistic features, such as tone of voice, gesture and posture.
zh: 好，今天的讲座讨论了一些副语言特征，例如语气、手势和姿态。

en: These features, together with linguistic features of language, like grammar, or vocabulary,
zh: 这些特征，与语法、词汇等语言特征一起，

en: are all part of the way we communicate with each other in face to face encounters.
zh: 都构成了面对面交流方式的一部分。

en: In our next lecture, we’ll watch some video material,
zh: 下一堂课，我们会看一些视频材料，

en: and see how people actually use paralinguistic means in communication to express their intention or desire or mood.
zh: 了解人们在交流中如何实际运用副语言手段，来表达意图、愿望或情绪。

en: Now you have three minutes to check your work.
zh: 现在你有三分钟检查作答。

en: This is the end of section A mini-lecture.
zh: A节短讲到此结束。
